children: Analysts cut NVIDIA price targets: Mizuho to $250, President Capital to $295, Citi to $285 and Wells Fargo to $300. Shares were 28% below their Oct. 6 record ahead of Nov. 17 earnings.
Reports allege a Chinese intelligence operative may have worked at NVIDIA for years and leaked company information. The scope of any leak and whether it reached Beijing remain unclear.
Wedbush kept NVIDIA (NVDA) at Outperform with a $300 target, contingent on CEO Jensen Huang staying. Analyst Dan Ives sees a 15% chance of Huang’s removal; shares could initially drop 25%–30%.
NVIDIA Corporation (NVDA) was expected to report fiscal fourth-quarter results on Nov. 17, with analysts estimating revenue of $109.17 billion and earnings per share of about $2.48.
Sen. Kevin Cramer called for NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang to resign, citing national-security concerns over reported ties to a woman suspected of working for Chinese intelligence.
On Nov. 10, Bank of America removed NVIDIA from its top-conviction US 1 list but kept its Buy rating. The bank gave no reason for the change.
U.S. House Republicans are considering issuing a subpoena to NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang, according to ABC News.
An article highlights uncertainty over NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang’s eventual successor, noting CFO Colette Kress as a possible interim leader but no clear permanent replacement.
Ahead of NVIDIA’s Nov. 17, 2026, fiscal Q3 results, Citi flagged investor questions on 2028 orders, backlog conversion, supply limits, the Rubin ramp and an investigation involving CEO Jensen Huang.
Analysts say the investigation could heighten scrutiny of NVIDIA’s China exposure, U.S. export controls and ties to MegaSpeed, including CEO Jensen Huang’s knowledge of the relationship.
